name: Chongqing Adolescent Twin Study (CATS)
description: A multimodal MRI and phenotyping resource from 136 typically developing twins aged 12-19, designed to separate genetic from environmental influences on adolescent brain and behaviour. Imaging covers structural, resting-state functional and diffusion MRI; the non-imaging battery spans cognitive ability, emotional and social behaviour, familial and parenting dynamics, sleep, stress, anxiety and depression. Benchmarked against HCP-Development, CATS meets or exceeds it on signal quality, tissue contrast, sharpness and head-motion control, and phenotype correlations with HCP-D support reliability. Preprocessed imaging phenotypes are provided. Distributed by the Brain Science Data Center of the Chinese Academy of Sciences; access requires a request following the instructions in the paper's Usage Notes.
citation: Zhu Y, Fu Y, Han J, Wang R, Ma X, et al. (2025). The Chongqing Adolescent Twin Study: An Integrative Multimodal Brain Imaging and Non-imaging Dataset. Scientific Data, 12, 1211.
